status: exact shared kinetic-shell count and matrix-free nonlinear solver plan

integralEquivalence.bijection: m=K^-1 n in Z^8, n=K m
integralEquivalence.consequence: both conditional charging branches have the same kinetic energy multiplicities and can use one E8-shell enumerator

thetaSeries.normConvention: shell m has squared E8 norm 2m and kinetic energy m when H_kin=Q/2

commonBasisDifferentOperators.commonKineticBasis: integer m ordered by m^T K m/2 and truncated by complete E8 shells
commonBasisDifferentOperators.cartanKernelPotentialSteps: m maps to m plus or minus e_i
commonBasisDifferentOperators.inverseKernelPotentialSteps: m maps to m plus or minus K^-1 e_i
commonBasisDifferentOperators.interpretation: the two models share diagonal kinetic energies but have different sparse hopping graphs; topology has not made their dynamics equivalent

solverPlan.representation: hash-indexed complete E8 shells with matrix-free symmetric matvec
observables: transition weights under eight local drives
solverPlan.stabilityGate: promote a level only when successive complete-shell cutoffs agree inside the preregistered tolerance and its boundary probability or residual decreases

established: The joined nonlinear problem does not require an anisotropic Cartesian box. Exact E8 theta coefficients give the basis size in advance, and the K/K^-1 hypotheses can be compared on one kinetic carrier by changing only the sixteen potential transitions.
boundary: This packet sizes and compiles the sparse problem; it does not report converged nonlinear eigenvalues. A projected finite-shell eigenvalue is variational data, not yet the continuum gap. The inverse step set is not operator-complete before shell 15.
nextGate: implement the common-shell enumerator and matrix-free lowest-eigenpair solver, then publish the first cutoff convergence table for both step sets
